opportunities.title: Replace math questions with a 200-question history event bank
opportunities.summary: ## Goal Change the core choice mechanic from equations to chronological history comparisons. Present two historical events and ask the player which happened later. ## Scope - Create a data-driven HistoryQuestion model independent of gates and crowd logic. - Include event title, year/date, short context, category, difficulty, and answer metadata. - Build a curated bank of at least 200 historically accurate comparisons. - Cover multiple regions and periods rather than focusing on a single country. - Support BCE/CE dates and avoid ambiguous same-year comparisons. - Randomize which event appears on the left/right. - Show a short explanation with both dates after the choice. - Avoid repeats during one level where possible. - Keep data easy to review and edit, preferably through ScriptableObjects or JSON imported into Unity. ## Acceptance criteria - A gate pair displays two readable event choices. - The prompt clearly asks which event happened later. - Correct and wrong choices retain the existing crowd reward/penalty behavior. - At least 200 reviewed questions are included. - Every answer can be verified from the stored event dates. - The bank is separated from scene and crowd code.

opportunities.title: parse_duration drops the days (d) unit
opportunities.summary: ## Bug `parse_duration` silently drops the **days** (`d`) unit. The README lists `d` as a supported unit, but the parser ignores it and returns a wrong (too-small) result instead of raising or counting it. ### Reproduction ```python from duration_utils import parse_duration parse_duration("1d") # -> 0 (expected 86400) parse_duration("2d4h") # -> 14400 (expected 187200) ``` ### Expected `d` should be counted as 86400 seconds, so `parse_duration("1d") == 86400` and `parse_duration("2d4h") == 187200`. ### Notes The `d` character is already accepted by the token regex, so malformed-input detection still passes — the value is just never added. A fix should add the `d` unit and cover it with tests. /bounty $50
